title: The eraser's share in LSK progenitors read
set_out: Read PHY-090 by its sealed rule; keep deriving each cell type's level; keep heavy work off the laptop.
open_at_turnover: Each cell type's level (A8): donor age and the governor lead; the book cross-references (author's yes); the qubit floor constants (private).

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: The eraser's share in LSK progenitors (PHY-090)
entries.what: Six GSE72630 libraries on GitHub at the sealed depth, scored once by the sealed rule.
entries.outcome: On watch: knockout over wild type 0.951 against 0.86 (pull +2.59), null test clean; P8 (exploration) wild types spread less than knockouts.

entries.what: Two measured inputs added to the cell simulator, with six self-tests.
entries.outcome: 23 of 23 self-tests pass; the law's thermal level plus each type's eraser share; stray marks from one selection step.

entries.title: The within-sample slope from the derived hold (PHY-087, A7)
entries.what: Prediction written first (cooperative maintenance through the derived pump), then the eleven measured within-sample slopes read.
entries.outcome: Median measured 0.0551 against 0.0369-0.0398 predicted, inside the band written first; at each sample's own looseness median ratio 0.93 (ten samples).

entries.title: Is the eraser the cell's proofreading? (A18)
entries.what: Two branches written first, then the stray-mark counts of five committed knockout units read.
entries.outcome: Knockout over wild type 0.985-1.292: one selection step; the eraser is not proofreading the unmarked side.

entries.what: The first laboratory re-read at tiles of 2,000 to 50,000 CpGs; step 2's canary scored by its rule.
entries.outcome: Median ratio 0.93 to 1.37 with tile size (within the band written first, not 7 %); step 2 canary NOT MET at 2,000 CpGs, redesigned at 50,000.

entries.what: The blind-test laboratory's 54 libraries recounted by the chain from saved molecules and read on GitHub by the pipeline.
entries.outcome: Within-sample ratio median 1.03 (0.34-1.67), inside the first laboratory's range; across types 2.4 times steeper than the form, as in the first laboratory.

entries.title: E(a) and the exponent 7/2 read over the whole history (X7)
entries.what: Desk derivation, sympy and a full LCDM numeric check (x7_two_histories.py, x7_relative_growth.py).
entries.outcome: The rate accounting with n = 7/2 and the first law with the record term agree only at a = 1; over the history they disagree (n_eff = 19/2 + 1/a). E(a) rests on the record constraint, which is the balance law d ln E/d ln a = 1 - ln E (writer at one per e-fold, no eraser). The chains, which use E(a) as the record term's shape, are unchanged. Book: note added at eq:law_Sneed.
entries.reference: none (not a reading against healthy): cosmology derivation

entries.title: Who writes the cosmic record: baryons only or all matter (R4)
entries.what: The book's free-coupling fit (ten published numbers), already run; no new data.
entries.outcome: All matter writing (beta_m = Omega_m/2) sits at -0.09 sigma from the free value 0.155 +/- 0.029; baryons only (Omega_b/2 = 0.025) is excluded at 4.5 sigma. Book: note added in the cosmological-constant chapter.
entries.reference: none (not a reading against healthy): cosmology derivation

entries.title: Can halo virialization supply beta_m? (X6)
entries.what: Two desk counts, energy and bits (x6_bit_count.py).
entries.outcome: Halo kinetic energy is 2.6e-8 to 2.6e-6 of the critical energy against beta_m = 0.158: about a millionth. The size Omega_m/2 is that of matter's binding at the horizon scale (G M_H/(R_H c^2) = 1/2). Which process supplies the amount is open. Book: note added in the cosmological-coupling chapter.

entries.title: The virial share for driven systems (R1)
entries.outcome: Clausius' theorem needs only a stationary system; measured halo surface pressure (10-20 % of binding) shows cosmic structure is driven; the sign of the shift in the written share is not fixed by energy flow alone.
